entries.title: Psalms 124:1
segments:
. The writer, for the Church, praises God for past, and expresses trust for future, deliverance from foes. 
 
    1, 2. on our side--for us (

entries.title: Psalms 124:3
segments:
3. Then--that is, the time of our danger. 
 
    quick--literally, "living" (

entries.title: Psalms 124:5
segments: 5. The epithet proud added to waters denotes insolent enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 124:6
segments: 6, 7. The figure is changed to that of a rapacious wild beast (
), complete escape is denoted by breaking the net.

entries.title: Psalms 124:8
segments: ). He thus places over against the great danger the omnipotent God, and drowns, as it were in an anthem, the wickedness of the whole world and of hell, just as a great fire consumes a little drop of water [LUTHER].
